messages.subject: Skewed segregation and stepwiseqtl problem
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have a couple of problems with QTL mapping in a tomato RIL population (130 individuals) genotyped with sequencing data (GBS and RNAseq) with about 2500 genomic bins:

I have a couple of regions (on different chromosomes) with strongly skewed segregation (probably due to bushy phenotypic selection). One is about 2% genotype B and the other one is about 10% genotype A. That cause me artificial QTLs in a stepwiseqtl analysis. Do you think it will be wise to not using these markers? Do you have other suggestions?
The stepwiseqtl analysis tends sometimes to split a qtl into 2 adjacent qtls. It adds 2 (or more) markers (their names are as the original markers with “1” addition) adjacent to the marker with the highest lod score (I got that from the attribute “lodprofile”). One of them has a zero lod, and the other has a lod similar to the original qtl. That cause 2 adjacent qtls. Any idea why is that happening and if (and how) it can be solved?

I would appreciate any help with these,

Thanks, Itay

messages.subject: backward elimination in MQM for 4 way cross
messages.subject_clean: backward elimination in MQM for 4 way cross
messages.body_plain:
Dear Karl and others,

I am manipulating a F2 outcross, which corresponds to 4 way cross using r/qtl. As I understood from the previous posts, the function stepwiseqtl doesn't handle 4 way cross properly so far.

So instead, I built the MQM model (makeqtl), optimized the model (refineqtl) and then search for additional additive QTL (addqtl). I considered both 0.05 and 0.2 significance level from the scanone permutation test as threshold for additional QTL. Then when evaluating the new (optimized by refineqtl) MQM including the added additional QTL, I can only use the command fitqtl to perform a drop one analysis to see if any QTLs should be eliminated. However, I wonder such approach for backward elimination is appropriate, as the QTLs' positions are optimized for the full MQM, not for MQM dropping one QTL. Therefore, the comparison between the full MQM and MQM dropping one QTL might be biased. Unfortenately, I didn't find a good solution in the book or any other instruction materials on r/qtl.

I would be very grateful if you have any ideas about better way of performing model comparisons for backward elimination in MQM.

Thank you a lot!

Xiaodong

messages.body_plain:
Hi there,
I want to use R/qtl to perform linkage analysis of a mouse bakcross. I have the SNP genotyping data and I want to compare the estimated genetic map from my data to the reference genetic map. In past experiments I converted the SNP positions in base pairs to centiMorgan using the mouse map converter: http://cgd.jax.org/mousemapconverter/
But it seems that the server is not working. I have been looking for other tools to do this, but I did not find any. Any information about this topic would be really helpful.

Kind regards

I'm not completely sure what you mean by bias in this context. You're fitting and comparing a series of models. Key questions are how to compare models, and then whether you are evaluating all of the ones you'd like to evaluate?

messages.subject: scan additional interacting QTLs by addqtl
messages.subject_clean: scan additional interacting QTLs by addqtl
messages.body_plain:
Hi Karl and other community members,

I have a question about threshold for scanning additional interacting QTLs. The code below is the sample code from the r/qtl book, which tries to search for additional QTL interacting with Q4

> out.aq <http://out.aq> <- addqtl(hyper, qtl=rqtl, formula=y~Q1+Q2+Q3*Q4)

messages.body_plain:
I don't yet have a way to write out the data for R/qtl2.

And I wouldn't recommend using qtl2cl at this point; that's being explored as a way to make an command-line-based "API" for R/qtl2, particularly for GeneNetwork2 (http://gn2.genenetwork.org/).

messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl-disc] RQTL2 questions; LOD plot marker ticks, lod scores manipulation and citation preferences...
messages.body_plain:
> 1) I'm preparing my LOD plots for the chromosomes of interest, however I haven't been able to include "ticks" in marker positions as the ones in RQTL. Do you have any trick that can help me with that issue?

The data vis part of R/qtl2 is not yet well developed. And I had in mind mostly high-dimensional data, where the marker ticks end up being a big black bar.

In the short term, probably the easiest thing is to use qtl2convert::scan_qtl2_to_qtl() to convert the genome scan calculated by R/qtl2 into the format used by R/qtl1, and then use the R/qtl1 functions to make your plot.

> 2) I have 7 years of data for 2 traits (24 traits in the model). As summary plot, I would like to average the 7 LOD scores for each trait and use the average in a "summary" LOD plot. I have been able to export the scan1 result (with LOCO) to an excel file with the LOD score at each position (pseudo markers + markers). But I haven't been able to, after adding the averages, make a plot using the map with pseudo markers created by the program.
>
> For now I exported the map and scan1 results, so I can work on them and map using another program. However I would like to have the figure with the same nice format of the ones created by plot_scan1...

It requires a bit of messing about, but I'd try calculating the averages within R. The main trick is preserving the "scan1" class and other attributes.

library(qtl2geno)
library(qtl2scan)
iron <- read_cross2(system.file("extdata", "iron.zip", package="qtl2geno"))
Xcovar <- get_x_covar(iron)
map <- insert_pseudomarkers(iron$gmap, step=1)
pr <- calc_genoprob(iron, map)
out <- scan1(pr, iron$pheno, Xcovar=Xcovar)

# make a copy of the scan1 output
out_avelod <- out
# replace the first column with the row means
out_avelod[,1] <- rowMeans(out)
# change the name
colnames(out_avelod)[1] <- "aveLOD"

# cbind the original results with the first column of the copy
out <- cbind(out, subset(out_avelod, lod=1))

> 3) Is there any article to reference RQTL2? I know is fairly new, but I wander if you have any preferred way to cite it...

Not yet. I guess just cite the website, http://kbroman.org/qtl2

kind regards,
karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] scan additional interacting QTL
messages.body_plain:
There are two approaches for this:

First, you can pull out the genotypes for a marker near the QTL, and use that as an additive covariate in scanone(). With f4 data, you'd need to turn the marker genotypes into a two-column matrix of genotypes. To scan for interactive QTL, use the marker genotypes as an interactive covariate.

Alternatively, you can use makeqtl() and addqtl(). To scan for interactive QTL, you'll need to use a formula like y ~ Q1*Q2.

See http://rqtl.org/tutorials/rqtltour.pdf: steps 4-6 in Example 5 Multiple QTL mapping, pg 14
And the R/qtl book (http://rqtl.org/book), pages 206-208.

karl
